html:
The Kukatj are an Aboriginal Australian people of the plains south of the Gulf of Carpentaria in Queensland. They are not the same as the Kukatja of Western Australia or the Luritja of the Northern Territory, who were also once called Kukatja. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is flat land crossed by rivers running north into the Gulf, with wet season floods and dry season waterholes. Little is recorded of them in detail. Neighbours on the map include the Mingin, the Gkuthaarn and the Mayi Kutuna. Cattle stations took over the region from the 1860s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
